Hey there, so currently this repo is in a really good state. I had you build it from the ground up as an implementation of a very high-quality pair of papers. You can take a look at the documentation if you want, but essentially this is designed to be a scalable, highly modular engine for running factor graphs on hardware accelerators.

So the thing that I would like to focus on in this session is essentially a plotting facility that will be able to produce visual plots for the graphs that the engine generates. So what is this component going to be used for? Certainly, it can be used for generating SVG or PNG for quick previews of what a model looks like, but eventually we will also want to use it in a programmatic context, such as in a GUI or potentially an interactive GUI.

I'm not sure. I think the interactive GUI is going to be its own thing, to be honest. Right now, we just want plotting functionality.  So the nice thing here is that the paper, especially paper 1 of the pair, which is in the notes section, essentially defines a visual algebra for making these graphs. What the paper includes is a boxes and wires sort of diagram, where the shape of the wire is meaningful, and the position of beads along the wires are meaningful, as well as the text inside of the nodes. And I would also say that the boxes and wires are laid out sort of on an invisible grid, so that there is a very tidy sort of rectilinear look and feel.

Edges can be terminated by a black square that indicates a constraint, such as data, at the end of a wire. And then for rollouts, we would probably want to indicate that things can be rolled out using an ellipsis. And so, following human conventions of understanding the visual field, time would tend to flow from left to right if there is a time component.

The thing is that these graphs don't have a native understanding of time, so I think we would just have a bias towards things that are glued together, that is, rollouts, just having a left-to-right flow unless they otherwise can't flow that way.

And one other desideratum for this renderer is that if a graph is modified with the addition of some box and wire, then the resulting image should probably have very minimal changes to it. That way, if a graph is slowly built up, then the image representing each stage of that editing process should be very visually similar in terms of its layout.

And so, there's going to have to be some kind of ordered way of laying out the graph. So you may want to use a visual facility for looking at the diagrams in the paper, but I think I will copy-paste a couple here to give you the flavor of it.  In fact, the specific diagrams you should look for are Figure 14, which shows the uncompressed graph, Figure 15, which shows removing empty beads from chains, Figure 16, which shows removing beads on nodes with default factorization, Figure 17, removing internal edges, Figure 18, which is pushing beads to node borders, Figure 19, which shows the full compression.

I would also look at Figure 22, Figure 23, Figure 24, Figure 26, and Figure 27, and Figure 29 for additional examples. Since there is a logical order to these compression steps, and sort of, like, some of them represent just ways of making the graph easier to look at, there should be options for rendering the graph with different levels of compression, which are illustrated in those figures I discussed and also explained in the paper. So, in conclusion, please take a look and let me know if you have any questions. I would also recommend looking at the tickets and using that to sort of guide the way that you build this. Super excited to get started on this.

# cffg

Constrained Forney-style Factor Graphs (CFFG) and Lagrangian Active Inference
(LAIF) in JAX — an engine for building **white-box probabilistic agents**:
models you can read, edit, checkpoint, and ship, whose exploration comes from
their objective (Generalised Free Energy) rather than bolted-on noise.

Implements Koudahl, van de Laar & de Vries, *Realising Synthetic Active
Inference Agents* Parts I & II (arXiv:2306.08014), validated to 1.7e-6
against the authors' Julia reference on the T-maze benchmark.

```sh
uv sync          # install
uv run pytest    # 105 tests; the T-maze + gridworld suites are living examples
```

## The mental model

A model is a **Template**: a factor graph (square factors, edges = variables)
plus **constraint beads** that pick the variational objective, plus typed
**ports** where the world plugs in.

| Piece | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `VariableSpec` | a discrete random variable (an edge; connects ≤ 2 factors) |
| `FactorSpec` | a distribution node: `categorical`, `matrix_cat`, `transition_mixture`, `equality`, `dirichlet` |
| `ConstraintSpec` | a bead: `P_SUBSTITUTION` (adds the epistemic/GFE drive), `DELTA` (MAP readout), `MEAN_FIELD` (VMP) |
| `PortSpec` | a dangling edge with a role: `data` (sensor), `goal`, `prior`, `glue` (composition) |

The load-bearing invariant: every variable is either fully connected or
exposed through exactly one port — so "no dangling edges" and "models
compose" are the same rule.

**The one bead that matters most:** `P_SUBSTITUTION` on an observation factor
facing a goal factor turns that pair into a GFE composite — the agent then
*values information* about that observation. Without it you get a KL-control
agent that never explores (we test this: same graph, one bead, 90% vs 0% on
the T-maze).

## Build a model

For the common case — a discrete POMDP over a time window — one call:

```python
import numpy as np
from cffg.models.rollout import build_rollout

template, arrays = build_rollout(
    "my_world",
    steps=3,          # slices in the window
    past=0,           # slices 1..past are perception (data ports act{k}/obs{k})
    d=d,              # prior over the initial state          [K]
    A=A,              # observation model, column-stochastic   [M, K]
    c=c,              # goal prior over observations           [M]
    e=e,              # control prior                          [U]
    Bs=Bs,            # per-control transitions, col-stochastic [U, K, K]
    gfe=True,         # P-beads on future observations (curiosity on)
)
```

`cffg.models.tmaze` and `cffg.models.gridworld` are two worked instances of
this. For custom topologies, build the `Template` by hand (see
`tests/conftest.py` for a hand-built HMM slice) and grow big models from
small ones:

```python
from cffg.core.compose import unroll, compose
chain = unroll(slice_template, 10, {"tail": "head"})     # glue-port chaining
model = compose(prior_template, chain, {"attach": "t0/head"}, name="hmm10")
```

## Run inference

```python
from cffg.compiler import compile_template
from cffg.engine import Engine

engine = Engine(compile_template(template, arrays=arrays))
state  = engine.init_state()
state  = engine.bind_data(state, {"obs1": 4, "obs2": None})   # clamp / missing

# Ergonomics: the P-bead footgun and friends

**Ticket:** cff-cj5h · **Priority:** medium · **Status:** not started

Context (from the ablation discussion with Cooper): omitting a P-bead is a
*silent-but-well-defined* failure — you get a coherent KL-control agent that
never explores, and nothing errors. Same UX class as forgetting
`requires_grad`. Humans will hit this; rigorous agents won't. Three
mitigations, in effort order:

## 1. Epistemic lint (small)

At compile time, warn when the model has goal factors on future/unclamped
observations but zero `P_SUBSTITUTION` beads: "this agent will not explore —
intended?" Warning, not error (KL-control is legitimate). Implementation:
a `lint(template) -> list[str]` in `cffg/core/` (keep the compiler quiet by
default; `compile_template(..., lint=True)` or a standalone call for GUIs —
`check_edits` + lint is the editor's live-validation pair). Also lint:
δ-beads on edges that are never hardened (harden_last=0 pipelines), and
mean-field beads that provably equal BP (single free edge).

## 2. MI-term diagnostic (small, high value)

The FE ledger is per-node; expose the decomposition instead of only the sum:
`engine.fe_breakdown(state) -> {node: term}` plus, for GFE composites, the
split of −z̄ᵀρ into extrinsic (Āᵀlog c part) vs epistemic (−log q_x − h̃
part). "How curious is my agent right now" becomes a printable number; the
dashboard could even chart it. This is mostly refactoring `_make_bfe` to
return a dict before summing.

## 3. MAP tie-breaking (tiny, do first)

`np.argmax` resolves ties to index 0 — which turned "indifferent" into
"frozen at the start position" for the ablation agent. Fix in
`RollingAgent.act` and anywhere else argmax picks actions: break exact ties
uniformly at random with the agent's own rng (deterministic given seed).
Keep a regression test: an agent with a perfectly symmetric posterior should
not always pick action 0.

Add a reusable library component that renders CFFG-style diagrams with deterministic layout, plus a script that walks experiments/ and creates a model diagram for each experiment artifact that lacks one.

Generated model_diagram.svg for all 17 existing experiment artifact folders; rerunning the script skips existing diagrams unless --overwrite is passed. 56	  uncommitted work or an un-updated ticket has failed its landing.
57	- **One ticket ≈ one context window.** If a ticket can't fit, split it before

# AGENTS.md — Ground Rules for the CFFG Project

This project is a collaboration with a user named Cooper.

This repository implements **Constrained Forney-style Factor Graphs (CFFGs)** and
**Lagrangian Active Inference (LAIF)** in JAX, following:

- *Realising Synthetic Active Inference Agents, Part I: Epistemic Objectives and
  Graphical Specification Language* (Koudahl, van de Laar, de Vries — arXiv:2306.08014)
- *Part II: Variational Message Updates* (van de Laar, Koudahl, de Vries)

Both papers live in `notes/` (PDFs plus extracted text). The project brief is in the
Obsidian vault at `agents/CFFG/0.0.md`. Reference implementation for parity testing:
https://github.com/biaslab/LAIF (Julia/RxInfer).

## Rules

1. **Package management: `uv` only.** Use `uv init`, `uv add`, `uv run`, `uv sync`.
   Never call `pip` directly, never hand-edit lockfiles. The venv is managed by uv.

2. **Atomic git commits.** One logical change per commit — a commit should build and
   pass tests on its own. Commit early and often; keep refactors separate from
   behavior changes. Reference ticket IDs in commit messages (e.g. `tk-42: ...`).

3. **Tickets via `tk`.** All work is tracked in the `tk` ticket system (`tk --help`
   for usage). Break work into small tickets with dependency links, use epics for the
   major milestones, and close tickets in the same session as the commit that
   resolves them. Before starting work, check `tk` for ready tickets.

4. **Act autonomously.** The agent has broad access to this machine and should use
   it: run tests, install deps, create tickets, commit, and keep moving without
   asking for permission on routine steps. Ask only for genuinely irreversible or
   scope-changing decisions.

5. **Side research goes to sub-agents.** When background reading is needed
   (downloading another paper, checking how PGMax allocates tensors, clarifying an
   active-inference derivation), spawn a sub-agent with the *specific questions* to
   answer and have it report back a short summary. Do not read whole papers into the
   main context window mid-task.

## Session protocol (context hygiene)

This project will span many context windows. The rule that makes that survivable:
**tickets are the shared memory; the repo carries no session state.**

- **Start of session**: read this file, run `tk ready`, pick ONE ticket (or a few
  trivially small ones). Don't re-derive project state from scratch — the ticket's
  description, design notes, and comments are the handoff.
- **During**: atomic commits referencing the ticket ID. Discovered work becomes a
  *new ticket* (linked with a dependency), not scope drift in the current one.
- **End of session**: run `uv run python tools/dashboard.py` to refresh the
  mobile test dashboard (~/agent-share/cffg-tests.html; add new test files to
  EPIC_FILES). Leave `main` green and the tree clean. Update the ticket with
  a handoff comment — what's done, what's next, any gotcha — then close it or leave
  it `in_progress` with that comment as the resume point. A session that ends with
  uncommitted work or an un-updated ticket has failed its landing.
- **One ticket ≈ one context window.** If a ticket can't fit, split it before
  starting, not after running out of context.

### Sub-agent research protocol

- Spawn research sub-agents with **specific questions**, not topics ("What update
  rule does PGMax use for factor-to-variable messages and how are its arenas
  indexed?" — not "read about PGMax").
- The sub-agent's report gets **distilled into the ticket that needed it** as a
  comment (question → answer → source → confidence). Durable engine-relevant
  conclusions go into docstrings next to the code they justify.
- Never paste a paper or long raw report into the main context; never let a
  sub-agent's full output become a new markdown file.

### Document policy

Four canonical documents: `AGENTS.md` (rules), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
(design), `docs/LIMITATIONS.md` (scope honesty), `README.md` (the user guide).
**Update in place; do not create new markdown files** — with one sanctioned
exception: `docs/todo-notes/` holds one note per *remaining* under-explained
work thread (per Cooper, 2026-07-05). Each note names its `tk` ticket; when
the work lands, **delete the note in the same commit** — todo-notes describe
the future only, never the present (the present belongs to README/
ARCHITECTURE/docstrings). Everything else lives in tickets (state,
decisions-in-progress, research findings), code docstrings (durable
knowledge), or tests (executable claims). If a decision changes the
architecture, edit ARCHITECTURE.md in the same commit as the change.

## Technical invariants

- **True Bethe/Generalised free energy.** No shortcuts in the objective: free-energy
  evaluation must follow the papers' definitions (node-local BFE terms, edge-entropy
  overcounting corrections, P-substitution for GFE nodes). FE values are the
  convergence signal and the policy-scoring quantity — treat them as first-class
  outputs, and test them against analytically known cases.
- **Messages in log-space** wherever feasible; normalize aggressively; explicit JAX
  PRNG keys for anything stochastic (e.g. importance-sampled messages) so runs are
  reproducible.
- **Serialization is the source of truth.** Model structure lives in the template
  format (no large blobs inline — blobs are file paths); the compiled JAX arena is a
  derived artifact and must always be reconstructible from the template + data.

1	"""CFFG intermediate representation.
2	
3	A Template is a Forney-style factor graph fragment (factors = nodes, variables =
4	edges) plus the constraint annotations that make it a *constrained* FFG
5	(Koudahl et al. 2023, §5): factorization/form constraints and P-substitution
6	markers that together specify the variational family Q and the free-energy
7	functional, not just the generative model f.
8	
9	Boundary edges are declared as typed ports. The port invariant (enforced by
10	cffg.core.validate) is the single mechanism behind unrolling, rollout gluing,
11	"no dangling edges," and template composition: every variable is either fully
12	connected (degree 2) or exposed through exactly one port.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
18	from enum import Enum
19	
20	
21	class PortRole(str, Enum):
22	    """What a dangling boundary edge is waiting for."""
23	
24	    DATA = "data"  # sensor clamp: observed one-hot value bound at runtime
25	    GOAL = "goal"  # goal prior over a future observation
26	    PRIOR = "prior"  # parameter/state prior factor
27	    GLUE = "glue"  # bonds to another template instance (unrolling, composition)
28	
29	
30	@dataclass(frozen=True)
31	class VariableSpec:
32	    """An edge in the FFG: a named random variable.
33	
34	    Discrete one-hot domains only for now; a continuous domain becomes an
35	    alternative to `cardinality` when Gaussian support lands (LIMITATIONS S1).
36	    """
37	
38	    name: str
39	    cardinality: int
40	
41	
42	@dataclass(frozen=True)
43	class BlobRef:
44	    """Named reference to an array stored outside the template (never inline)."""
45	
46	    name: str
47	    path: str  # relative to the bundle root
48	
49	
50	@dataclass(frozen=True)
51	class FactorSpec:
52	    """A node in the FFG.
53	
54	    `edges` maps the factor type's roles to variable names. `params` maps a
55	    parameter role to its source: an edge (learned, e.g. A under a Dirichlet
56	    prior) or a blob (fixed, e.g. the T-maze B matrices). Each parameter role
57	    must be bound by exactly one of the two.
58	    """
59	
60	    name: str
61	    type: str  # key into FACTOR_TYPES
62	    edges: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # role -> variable
63	    param_edges: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # role -> variable
64	    param_blobs: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # role -> blob name
65	
66	    def all_edges(self) -> dict[str, str]:
67	        """All connected variables by role, structural and parameter alike."""
68	        return {**self.edges, **self.param_edges}
69	
70	
71	class ConstraintKind(str, Enum):
72	    DELTA = "delta"  # pointmass form constraint on an edge marginal (MAP reads)
73	    MEAN_FIELD = "mean_field"  # naive factorization of a node marginal
74	    P_SUBSTITUTION = "p_substitution"  # q(x) -> p(x|rest); local VFE becomes GFE
75	    MOMENT_MATCHING = "moment_matching"  # reserved for EP; no rules registered yet
76	
77	
78	# Which kinds target an edge (variable name) vs a node (factor name).
79	EDGE_CONSTRAINTS = frozenset({ConstraintKind.DELTA})
80	NODE_CONSTRAINTS = frozenset(
81	    {ConstraintKind.MEAN_FIELD, ConstraintKind.P_SUBSTITUTION, ConstraintKind.MOMENT_MATCHING}
82	)
83	
84	
85	@dataclass(frozen=True)
86	class ConstraintSpec:
87	    kind: ConstraintKind
88	    target: str  # variable name (edge kinds) or factor name (node kinds)
89	    detail: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()
90	    # detail is a sorted tuple of key/value pairs so specs stay hashable and
91	    # canonically serializable, e.g. (("substituted_role", "out"),).
92	
93	    def detail_dict(self) -> dict[str, str]:
94	        return dict(self.detail)
95	
96	
97	@dataclass(frozen=True)
98	class PortSpec:
99	    name: str
100	    variable: str
101	    role: PortRole
102	
103	
104	@dataclass(frozen=True)
105	class FactorType:
106	    """Structural signature of a factor kind. Math lives in cffg.rules (M2+)."""
107	
108	    name: str
109	    edge_roles: tuple[str, ...]  # required structural edges
110	    param_roles: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # each bound by exactly one edge or blob
111	    symmetric_domain: bool = False  # all structural edges share one cardinality
112	
113	
114	FACTOR_TYPES: dict[str, FactorType] = {}
115	
116	
117	def register_factor_type(ft: FactorType) -> FactorType:
118	    if ft.name in FACTOR_TYPES:
119	        raise ValueError(f"factor type {ft.name!r} already registered")
120	    overlap = set(ft.edge_roles) & set(ft.param_roles)
121	    if overlap:
122	        raise ValueError(f"factor type {ft.name!r}: roles {sorted(overlap)} are both edge and param")
123	    FACTOR_TYPES[ft.name] = ft
124	    return ft
125	
126	
127	# The discrete vocabulary of the papers (Part II §5, Part I App. C).
128	register_factor_type(FactorType("categorical", edge_roles=("out",), param_roles=("statistic",)))
129	register_factor_type(FactorType("matrix_cat", edge_roles=("out", "in"), param_roles=("matrix",)))
130	register_factor_type(
131	    FactorType("transition_mixture", edge_roles=("out", "in", "selector"), param_roles=("matrices",))
132	)
133	register_factor_type(FactorType("dirichlet", edge_roles=("out",), param_roles=("counts",)))
134	register_factor_type(FactorType("equality", edge_roles=("a", "b", "c"), symmetric_domain=True))
135	
136	
137	@dataclass
138	class Template:
139	    """A CFFG fragment: the unit of serialization, composition, and compilation."""
140	
141	    name: str
142	    variables: dict[str, VariableSpec] = field(default_factory=dict)
143	    factors: dict[str, FactorSpec] = field(default_factory=dict)
144	    constraints: list[ConstraintSpec] = field(default_factory=list)
145	    ports: dict[str, PortSpec] = field(default_factory=dict)
146	    blobs: dict[str, BlobRef] = field(default_factory=dict)
147	    schema_version: str = "1"
148	
149	    def degree(self, variable: str) -> int:
150	        """Number of factor endpoints attached to an edge (FFG max is 2)."""
151	        return sum(
152	            1 for f in self.factors.values() for v in f.all_edges().values() if v == variable
153	        )
154	
155	    def ports_of(self, variable: str) -> list[PortSpec]:
156	        return [p for p in self.ports.values() if p.variable == variable]
157

edges) plus the constraint annotations that make it a *constrained* FFG
(Koudahl et al. 2023, §5): factorization/form constraints and P-substitution
markers that together specify the variational family Q and the free-energy
functional, not just the generative model f.

Boundary edges are declared as typed ports. The port invariant (enforced by
cffg.core.validate) is the single mechanism behind unrolling, rollout gluing,
"no dangling edges," and template composition: every variable is either fully
connected (degree 2) or exposed through exactly one port.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum


class PortRole(str, Enum):
    """What a dangling boundary edge is waiting for."""

    DATA = "data"  # sensor clamp: observed one-hot value bound at runtime
    GOAL = "goal"  # goal prior over a future observation
    PRIOR = "prior"  # parameter/state prior factor
    GLUE = "glue"  # bonds to another template instance (unrolling, composition)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class VariableSpec:
    """An edge in the FFG: a named random variable.

    Discrete one-hot domains only for now; a continuous domain becomes an
    alternative to `cardinality` when Gaussian support lands (LIMITATIONS S1).
    """

    name: str
    cardinality: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BlobRef:
    """Named reference to an array stored outside the template (never inline)."""

    name: str
    path: str  # relative to the bundle root


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FactorSpec:
    """A node in the FFG.

    `edges` maps the factor type's roles to variable names. `params` maps a
    parameter role to its source: an edge (learned, e.g. A under a Dirichlet
    prior) or a blob (fixed, e.g. the T-maze B matrices). Each parameter role
    must be bound by exactly one of the two.
    """

    name: str
    type: str  # key into FACTOR_TYPES
    edges: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # role -> variable
    param_edges: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # role -> variable
    param_blobs: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # role -> blob name

    def all_edges(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """All connected variables by role, structural and parameter alike."""
        return {**self.edges, **self.param_edges}


class ConstraintKind(str, Enum):
    DELTA = "delta"  # pointmass form constraint on an edge marginal (MAP reads)
    MEAN_FIELD = "mean_field"  # naive factorization of a node marginal
    P_SUBSTITUTION = "p_substitution"  # q(x) -> p(x|rest); local VFE becomes GFE
    MOMENT_MATCHING = "moment_matching"  # reserved for EP; no rules registered yet


# Which kinds target an edge (variable name) vs a node (factor name).
EDGE_CONSTRAINTS = frozenset({ConstraintKind.DELTA})
NODE_CONSTRAINTS = frozenset(
    {ConstraintKind.MEAN_FIELD, ConstraintKind.P_SUBSTITUTION, ConstraintKind.MOMENT_MATCHING}
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ConstraintSpec:
    kind: ConstraintKind
    target: str  # variable name (edge kinds) or factor name (node kinds)
    detail: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()
    # detail is a sorted tuple of key/value pairs so specs stay hashable and
    # canonically serializable, e.g. (("substituted_role", "out"),).

    def detail_dict(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        return dict(self.detail)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PortSpec:
    name: str
    variable: str
    role: PortRole


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FactorType:
    """Structural signature of a factor kind. Math lives in cffg.rules (M2+)."""

    name: str
    edge_roles: tuple[str, ...]  # required structural edges
    param_roles: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # each bound by exactly one edge or blob
    symmetric_domain: bool = False  # all structural edges share one cardinality


FACTOR_TYPES: dict[str, FactorType] = {}


def register_factor_type(ft: FactorType) -> FactorType:
    if ft.name in FACTOR_TYPES:
        raise ValueError(f"factor type {ft.name!r} already registered")
    overlap = set(ft.edge_roles) & set(ft.param_roles)
    if overlap:
        raise ValueError(f"factor type {ft.name!r}: roles {sorted(overlap)} are both edge and param")
    FACTOR_TYPES[ft.name] = ft
    return ft


# The discrete vocabulary of the papers (Part II §5, Part I App. C).
register_factor_type(FactorType("categorical", edge_roles=("out",), param_roles=("statistic",)))
register_factor_type(FactorType("matrix_cat", edge_roles=("out", "in"), param_roles=("matrix",)))
register_factor_type(
    FactorType("transition_mixture", edge_roles=("out", "in", "selector"), param_roles=("matrices",))
)
register_factor_type(FactorType("dirichlet", edge_roles=("out",), param_roles=("counts",)))
register_factor_type(FactorType("equality", edge_roles=("a", "b", "c"), symmetric_domain=True))


@dataclass
class Template:
    """A CFFG fragment: the unit of serialization, composition, and compilation."""

    name: str
    variables: dict[str, VariableSpec] = field(default_factory=dict)
    factors: dict[str, FactorSpec] = field(default_factory=dict)
    constraints: list[ConstraintSpec] = field(default_factory=list)
    ports: dict[str, PortSpec] = field(default_factory=dict)
    blobs: dict[str, BlobRef] = field(default_factory=dict)
    schema_version: str = "1"

    def degree(self, variable: str) -> int:
        """Number of factor endpoints attached to an edge (FFG max is 2)."""
        return sum(
            1 for f in self.factors.values() for v in f.all_edges().values() if v == variable
        )

    def ports_of(self, variable: str) -> list[PortSpec]:
        return [p for p in self.ports.values() if p.variable == variable]

1	"""Deterministic SVG diagrams for CFFG templates.
2	
3	The renderer is intentionally dependency-free. It lays out factors, variables,
4	parameter blobs, constraints, and ports on stable lanes inside a fixed-aspect
5	viewBox so small structural changes tend to appear as local visual changes.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	from dataclasses import dataclass
11	from html import escape
12	from pathlib import Path
13	import re
14	from statistics import median
15	
16	from cffg.core.ir import Template
17	
18	
19	@dataclass(frozen=True)
20	class DiagramStyle:
21	    width: int = 1280
22	    height: int = 720
23	    margin_x: float = 90.0
24	    margin_y: float = 70.0
25	    column_gap: float = 620.0
26	    row_gap: float = 58.0
27	    node_width: float = 132.0
28	    node_height: float = 34.0
29	    font_family: str = "Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, sans-serif"
30	
31	
32	@dataclass(frozen=True)
33	class _Node:
34	    key: str
35	    kind: str
36	    label: str
37	    detail: str
38	    column: int
39	    order: str
40	
41	
42	@dataclass(frozen=True)
43	class _Edge:
44	    source: str
45	    target: str
46	    label: str
47	    kind: str = "structural"
48	
49	
50	def render_template_svg(template: Template, *, style: DiagramStyle = DiagramStyle()) -> str:
51	    """Render `template` as a standalone SVG string.
52	
53	    Layout is deterministic: node columns come from scoped time suffixes when
54	    available, otherwise from sorted connectivity. Nodes use fixed lanes by
55	    semantic kind, and the SVG viewBox expands while the visible aspect ratio
56	    remains fixed through `preserveAspectRatio`.
57	    """
58	
59	    nodes, edges = _diagram_graph(template)
60	    positions, view_w, view_h = _layout(nodes, style)
61	    return _render_svg(template.name, nodes, edges, positions, view_w, view_h, style)
62	
63	
64	def save_template_svg(
65	    template: Template,
66	    path: str | Path,
67	    *,
68	    style: DiagramStyle = DiagramStyle(),
69	    overwrite: bool = True,
70	) -> bool:
71	    """Write a template diagram. Returns False when skipped by `overwrite=False`."""
72	
73	    out = Path(path)
74	    if out.exists() and not overwrite:
75	        return False
76	    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
77	    out.write_text(render_template_svg(template, style=style))
78	    return True
79	
80	
81	def _diagram_graph(template: Template) -> tuple[list[_Node], list[_Edge]]:
82	    columns: dict[str, int] = {}
83	    for name in template.variables:
84	        columns[f"var:{name}"] = _column_from_name(name)
85	    for name, factor in template.factors.items():
86	        connected = [columns.get(f"var:{v}", _column_from_name(v)) for v in factor.all_edges().values()]
87	        columns[f"factor:{name}"] = int(round(median(connected))) if connected else _column_from_name(name)
88	    for name, port in template.ports.items():
89	        columns[f"port:{name}"] = columns.get(f"var:{port.variable}", _column_from_name(port.variable))
90	    for name, blob in template.blobs.items():
91	        users = [
92	            columns[f"factor:{factor.name}"]
93	            for factor in template.factors.values()
94	            if name in factor.param_blobs.values()
95	        ]
96	        columns[f"blob:{name}"] = int(round(median(users))) if users else _column_from_name(blob.name)
97	    for i, constraint in enumerate(template.constraints):
98	        target_key = (
99	            f"factor:{constraint.target}"
100	            if constraint.target in template.factors
101	            else f"var:{constraint.target}"
102	        )
103	        columns[f"constraint:{i}"] = columns.get(target_key, _column_from_name(constraint.target))
104	
105	    nodes: list[_Node] = []
106	    for name, blob in sorted(template.blobs.items()):
107	        nodes.append(_Node(f"blob:{name}", "blob", name, blob.path, columns[f"blob:{name}"], name))
108	    for i, constraint in enumerate(template.constraints):
109	        detail = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in constraint.detail)
110	        nodes.append(
111	            _Node(
112	                f"constraint:{i}",
113	                "constraint",
114	                constraint.kind.value,
115	                f"{constraint.target}" + (f" | {detail}" if detail else ""),
116	                columns[f"constraint:{i}"],
117	                f"{constraint.kind.value}:{constraint.target}:{i}",
118	            )
119	        )
120	    for name, factor in sorted(template.factors.items()):
121	        nodes.append(
122	            _Node(
123	                f"factor:{name}",
124	                "factor",
125	                name,
126	                factor.type,
127	                columns[f"factor:{name}"],
128	                f"{_natural_key(name)}",
129	            )
130	        )
131	    for name, variable in sorted(template.variables.items()):
132	        detail = f"card {variable.cardinality}" if variable.cardinality > 0 else ""
133	        nodes.append(
134	            _Node(
135	                f"var:{name}",
136	                "variable",
137	                name,
138	                detail,
139	                columns[f"var:{name}"],
140	                f"{_natural_key(name)}",
141	            )
142	        )
143	    for name, port in sorted(template.ports.items()):
144	        nodes.append(
145	            _Node(
146	                f"port:{name}",
147	                "port",
148	                name,
149	                port.role.value,
150	                columns[f"port:{name}"],
151	                f"{port.role.value}:{_natural_key(name)}",
152	            )
153	        )
154	
155	    edges: list[_Edge] = []
156	    for factor in sorted(template.factors.values(), key=lambda f: _natural_key(f.name)):
157	        for role, variable in sorted(factor.edges.items()):
158	            edges.append((_factor_var_edge(factor.name, variable, role, "structural")))
159	        for role, variable in sorted(factor.param_edges.items()):
160	            edges.append((_factor_var_edge(factor.name, variable, role, "parameter")))
161	        for role, blob in sorted(factor.param_blobs.items()):
162	            edges.append(_Edge(f"blob:{blob}", f"factor:{factor.name}", role, "parameter"))
163	    for name, port in sorted(template.ports.items()):
164	        edges.append(_Edge(f"var:{port.variable}", f"port:{name}", port.role.value, "port"))
165	    for i, constraint in enumerate(template.constraints):
166	        target = (
167	            f"factor:{constraint.target}"
168	            if constraint.target in template.factors
169	            else f"var:{constraint.target}"
170	        )
171	        edges.append(_Edge(f"constraint:{i}", target, constraint.kind.value, "constraint"))
172	    return nodes, edges
173	
174	
175	def _factor_var_edge(factor: str, variable: str, role: str, kind: str) -> _Edge:
176	    return _Edge(f"factor:{factor}", f"var:{variable}", role, kind)
177	
178	
179	def _layout(
180	    nodes: list[_Node], style: DiagramStyle
181	) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[float, float]], float, float]:
182	    lanes = {
183	        "blob": 0,
184	        "constraint": 1,
185	        "factor": 2,
186	        "variable": 3,
187	        "port": 4,
188	    }
189	    x_offsets = {
190	        "blob": 0.0,
191	        "constraint": 100.0,
192	        "factor": 210.0,
193	        "variable": 410.0,
194	        "port": 560.0,
195	    }
196	    max_col = max((node.column for node in nodes), default=0)
197	    positions: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {}
198	    for kind, lane in lanes.items():
199	        by_col: dict[int, list[_Node]] = {}
200	        for node in nodes:
201	            if node.kind == kind:
202	                by_col.setdefault(node.column, []).append(node)
203	        for col, group in by_col.items():
204	            ordered = sorted(group, key=lambda n: n.order)
205	            x = style.margin_x + col * style.column_gap + x_offsets[kind]
206	            base_y = style.margin_y + lane * (style.row_gap * 2.0)
207	            for i, node in enumerate(ordered):
208	                positions[node.key] = (x, base_y + i * style.row_gap)
209	
210	    max_rows = 1
211	    for kind in lanes:
212	        for col in range(max_col + 1):
213	            max_rows = max(max_rows, sum(1 for n in nodes if n.kind == kind and n.column == col))
214	    content_w = style.margin_x * 2 + max_col * style.column_gap + style.node_width + 620
215	    content_h = style.margin_y * 2 + 5 * style.row_gap * 2 + max_rows * style.row_gap
216	    view_w = max(style.width, content_w)
217	    view_h = max(style.height, content_h)
218	    aspect = style.width / style.height
219	    if view_w / view_h < aspect:
220	        view_w = view_h * aspect
221	    else:
222	        view_h = view_w / aspect
223	    return positions, view_w, view_h
224	
225	
226	def _render_svg(
227	    title: str,
228	    nodes: list[_Node],
229	    edges: list[_Edge],
230	    positions: dict[str, tuple[float, float]],
231	    view_w: float,
232	    view_h: float,
233	    style: DiagramStyle,
234	) -> str:
235	    css = f"""
236	    .bg {{ fill: #fbfaf7; }}
237	    .title {{ font: 700 24px {style.font_family}; fill: #1f2933; }}
238	    .legend {{ font: 500 13px {style.font_family}; fill: #52606d; }}
239	    .node text {{ font-family: {style.font_family}; text-anchor: middle; }}
240	    .label {{ font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; fill: #17212b; }}
241	    .detail {{ font-size: 10px; fill: #52606d; }}
242	    .factor rect {{ fill: #e8f1ff; stroke: #2f68b7; }}
243	    .variable ellipse {{ fill: #f4f0ff; stroke: #7c5cc4; }}
244	    .blob path {{ fill: #eef8ef; stroke: #3b8a4b; }}
245	    .constraint rect {{ fill: #fff4df; stroke: #b7791f; stroke-dasharray: 5 3; }}
246	    .port rect {{ fill: #f4f6f8; stroke: #697386; }}
247	    .edge {{ fill: none; stroke: #7b8794; stroke-width: 1.4; }}
248	    .edge.parameter {{ stroke: #3b8a4b; stroke-dasharray: 4 3; }}
249	    .edge.constraint {{ stroke: #b7791f; stroke-dasharray: 5 4; }}
250	    .edge.port {{ stroke: #697386; stroke-dasharray: 2 4; }}
251	    .edge-label {{ font: 10px {style.font_family}; fill: #52606d; paint-order: stroke; stroke: #fbfaf7; stroke-width: 3px; }}
252	    """
253	    parts = [
254	        '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>',
255	        (
256	            f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{style.width}" '
257	            f'height="{style.height}" viewBox="0 0 {view_w:.0f} {view_h:.0f}" '
258	            'preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">'
259	        ),
260	        f"<style>{css}</style>",
261	        '<defs><marker id="arrow" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 Z" fill="#7b8794"/></marker></defs>',
262	        f'<rect class="bg" width="{view_w:.0f}" height="{view_h:.0f}"/>',
263	        f'<text class="title" x="32" y="42">{escape(title)}</text>',
264	        '<text class="legend" x="32" y="64">rect=factor  ellipse=variable  green=parameter/blob  dashed=constraint/port</text>',
265	    ]
266	
267	    for edge in sorted(edges, key=lambda e: (e.kind, e.source, e.target, e.label)):
268	        if edge.source not in positions or edge.target not in positions:
269	            continue
270	        x1, y1 = positions[edge.source]
271	        x2, y2 = positions[edge.target]
272	        y1 += style.node_height / 2
273	        y2 += style.node_height / 2
274	        mx, my = (x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2
275	        parts.append(
276	            f'<path class="edge {edge.kind}" marker-end="url(#arrow)" d="M{x1:.1f},{y1:.1f} C{mx:.1f},{y1:.1f} {mx:.1f},{y2:.1f} {x2:.1f},{y2:.1f}"/>'
277	        )
278	        if edge.label:
279	            parts.append(f'<text class="edge-label" x="{mx:.1f}" y="{my - 4:.1f}">{escape(edge.label)}</text>')
280	
281	    for node in sorted(nodes, key=lambda n: (n.kind, n.column, n.order)):
282	        x, y = positions[node.key]
283	        parts.append(_render_node(node, x, y, style))
284	    parts.append("</svg>\n")
285	    return "\n".join(parts)
286	
287	
288	def _render_node(node: _Node, x: float, y: float, style: DiagramStyle) -> str:
289	    w, h = style.node_width, style.node_height
290	    label = _shorten(node.label, 24)
291	    detail = _shorten(node.detail, 28)
292	    if node.kind == "variable":
293	        shape = f'<ellipse cx="{x:.1f}" cy="{y + h / 2:.1f}" rx="{w / 2:.1f}" ry="{h / 2:.1f}"/>'
294	    elif node.kind == "blob":
295	        shape = (
296	            f'<path d="M{x - w / 2:.1f},{y + 7:.1f} '
297	            f'C{x - w / 2:.1f},{y - 2:.1f} {x + w / 2:.1f},{y - 2:.1f} {x + w / 2:.1f},{y + 7:.1f} '
298	            f'L{x + w / 2:.1f},{y + h - 7:.1f} '
299	            f'C{x + w / 2:.1f},{y + h + 2:.1f} {x - w / 2:.1f},{y + h + 2:.1f} {x - w / 2:.1f},{y + h - 7:.1f} Z"/>'
300	        )
301	    else:
302	        rx = 12 if node.kind == "port" else 4
303	        shape = f'<rect x="{x - w / 2:.1f}" y="{y:.1f}" width="{w:.1f}" height="{h:.1f}" rx="{rx}"/>'
304	    detail_text = (
305	        f'<text class="detail" x="{x:.1f}" y="{y + 27:.1f}">{escape(detail)}</text>'
306	        if detail
307	        else ""
308	    )
309	    return (
310	        f'<g class="node {node.kind}">{shape}'
311	        f'<text class="label" x="{x:.1f}" y="{y + 16:.1f}">{escape(label)}</text>'
312	        f"{detail_text}</g>"
313	    )
314	
315	
316	def _shorten(text: str, max_chars: int) -> str:
317	    if len(text) <= max_chars:
318	        return text
319	    return text[: max_chars - 1] + "..."
320	
321	
322	def _column_from_name(name: str) -> int:
323	    if "/" in name:
324	        prefix = name.rsplit("/", 1)[0]
325	        match = re.search(r"(?:^|/)t(\d+)(?:/|$)", prefix)
326	        if match:
327	            return int(match.group(1))
328	    match = re.search(r"(\d+)$", name)
329	    return int(match.group(1)) if match else 0
330	
331	
332	def _natural_key(value: str) -> tuple[object, ...]:
333	    parts = re.split(r"(\d+)", value)
334	    return tuple(int(p) if p.isdigit() else p for p in parts)

options.description: Core stays dependency-free (SVG always works). `uv add --optional viz cairosvg`; save_png() raises a clear error if the extra isn't installed.

options.label: SVG only for now
options.description: Skip PNG entirely in v1; add it later when a concrete need appears (browsers, GUIs, and notebooks all render SVG natively).

options.label: Hard dependency
options.description: Add cairosvg as a regular dependency so PNG always works out of the box.

questions.question: The paper also draws message-passing schedules as small arrows along wires (Figs 23, 24, 27), with GFE messages in red. Should that overlay be part of this build, or a backlog ticket?

options.label: Backlog ticket (Recommended)
options.description: Design the scene graph so overlays can attach to wires later, but ship v1 as static structure rendering only. Keeps this session's scope to one solid component.

options.label: Include in v1
options.description: Render schedule arrows now, driven by the engine's message schedule. Bigger scope: needs a schedule→wire mapping and direction semantics.

questions.question: Which compression level should be the default when you just call render(template)?

options.label: Full compression (Recommended)
options.description: Level 4, like the paper's own figures for real models (Figs 22, 26). The paper calls compression 'mandatory' for practical use; uncompressed is available via an argument.

options.label: Uncompressed
options.description: Level 0 (Fig 14 style) — shows every bead explicitly; most faithful to the underlying variational spec but visually heavy for real models.

t1=$(tk create "viz: diagram IR — derive uncompressed CFFG annotation from Template" --parent cff-ql2n -p 1 -d "cffg/viz/scene.py-ish: typed diagram IR (FactorBox, Wire, Bead, Terminal, CompositeBox, Ellipsis marker), each carrying source Template element IDs. Derivation per Part I §5: default = joint internal bead per node + empty bead per edge, wires extended through borders for marginalisation; MEAN_FIELD -> per-edge border beads; DELTA -> ∂ bead on edge; data ports -> filled ∂ terminal; param_blobs -> black square terminals; P_SUBSTITUTION -> square bead on substituted role; GFE composite pairs (reuse compiler detection logic) -> dashed box.") && echo T1=$t1
t2=$(tk create "viz: compression passes 1-4 (p.19 recipe) on diagram IR" --parent cff-ql2n -p 1 -d "Four pure diagram->diagram transforms: (1) summarise bead chains by terminating beads; (2) remove empty internal beads on nodes with default factorisation; (3) remove internal edges on such nodes (careful: skip when a connected edge is pointmass in the model, cf. f_d in Fig 16/17); (4) push remaining internal beads to node borders. render level 0-4 selects prefix of passes; level 4 also shrinks boxes (Fig 19).") && echo T2=$t2
t3=$(tk create "viz: deterministic rectilinear grid layout, edit-stable" --parent cff-ql2n -p 1 -d "Integer-grid placement: columns from t{i}/ slice prefixes + glue-chain topology (time left-to-right); lanes per paper POMDP convention (param terminals above, state chain middle, obs/goal composites below); orthogonal wire routing. Stability: placement is an insertion-ordered function of stable names so adding a box/wire inserts a row/col and preserves all other relative positions.") && echo T3=$t3
t4=$(tk create "viz: SVG backend (paper style) + save_svg/save_png via optional extra" --parent cff-ql2n -p 1 -d "Scene graph -> SVG string, dependency-free: monochrome paper style, math-italic labels with subscripts (z_t), factor-type glyphs (Cat, T, TM, =, Dir), ellipsis for rollout continuation. save_png via cairosvg behind uv optional extra 'viz' with a clear ImportError message. Default compression level 4.") && echo T4=$t4
t5=$(tk create "viz: golden SVG tests + layout-stability regression" --parent cff-ql2n -p 2 -d "Golden files for tmaze, gridworld, hand-built HMM (conftest) at levels 0 and 4. Stability regression: add a factor+wire to a template, assert positions of pre-existing elements change only by the inserted row/col shift (relative order preserved). Add new test file to dashboard EPIC_FILES.") && echo T5=$t5
t6=$(tk create "viz: message-passing schedule overlay (Figs 23/24/27)" --parent cff-ql2n -p 3 -d "Backlog: arrows along wires from an engine schedule, GFE messages in red. Scene graph already anchors overlays to wires by source IDs.") && echo T6=$t6
tk dep $t2 $t1; tk dep $t3 $t1; tk dep $t4 $t3; tk dep $t4 $t2; tk dep $t5 $t4; tk dep $t6 $t4; tk start $t1

"""The generic discrete POMDP rollout template (the papers' Fig. 26 pattern).

One slice per timestep: control prior → transition mixture → equality branch
→ observation. The first `past` slices are perception-style (control and
observation exposed as DATA ports `act{k}` / `obs{k}`); the rest are
planning-style (control prior + P-substituted goal-observation composite).
As the agent's clock advances, a slice's beads flip from goal to data with
identical wiring — the receding-horizon constraint flip.

Any (d, A, c, e, Bs) instantiates it: the T-maze and the gridworld are both
one call away. Blob names are fixed (d/A/Ac/c/e/Bs) so runtimes can swap
parameters per tick via the params dict without recompiling.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from cffg.core.ir import (
    BlobRef,
    ConstraintKind,
    ConstraintSpec,
    FactorSpec,
    PortRole,
    PortSpec,
    Template,
    VariableSpec,
)


def build_rollout(
    name: str,
    *,
    steps: int,
    past: int = 0,
    d: np.ndarray,
    A: np.ndarray,
    c: np.ndarray,
    e: np.ndarray,
    Bs: np.ndarray,
    gfe: bool = True,
    map_policy: bool = False,
    learned_a: bool = False,
) -> tuple[Template, dict[str, np.ndarray]]:
    n_state, n_obs, n_ctrl = len(d), A.shape[0], len(e)
    assert Bs.shape == (n_ctrl, n_state, n_state), f"Bs shape {Bs.shape}"
    assert A.shape == (n_obs, n_state) and c.shape == (n_obs,)

    t = Template(name=name)
    t.blobs = {
        blob: BlobRef(blob, f"{blob}.npy") for blob in ("d", "A", "Ac", "c", "e", "Bs")
    }
    t.variables["z0"] = VariableSpec("z0", n_state)
    t.factors["prior"] = FactorSpec(
        "prior", "categorical", edges={"out": "z0"}, param_blobs={"statistic": "d"}
    )
    prev = "z0"
    for k in range(1, steps + 1):
        u, zm, zo, zt, x = f"u{k}", f"zm{k}", f"zo{k}", f"zt{k}", f"x{k}"
        t.variables |= {
            u: VariableSpec(u, n_ctrl),
            zm: VariableSpec(zm, n_state),
            zo: VariableSpec(zo, n_state),
            zt: VariableSpec(zt, n_state),
            x: VariableSpec(x, n_obs),
        }
        t.factors |= {
            f"tm{k}": FactorSpec(
                f"tm{k}", "transition_mixture",
                edges={"out": zm, "in": prev, "selector": u},
                param_blobs={"matrices": "Bs"},
            ),
            f"eq{k}": FactorSpec(f"eq{k}", "equality", edges={"a": zm, "b": zo, "c": zt}),
            f"obs{k}": FactorSpec(
                f"obs{k}", "matrix_cat", edges={"out": x, "in": zo},
                # Learned-A planning slices read Dirichlet counts ("Ac");
                # perception slices and fixed-A models read probabilities ("A").
                param_blobs={"matrix": "Ac" if (learned_a and k > past) else "A"},
            ),
        }
        if k <= past:  # perception slice: executed control + observed outcome
            t.ports[f"act{k}"] = PortSpec(f"act{k}", u, PortRole.DATA)
            t.ports[f"obs{k}"] = PortSpec(f"obs{k}", x, PortRole.DATA)
        else:  # planning slice: control prior + goal-constrained observation
            t.factors[f"e{k}"] = FactorSpec(
                f"e{k}", "categorical", edges={"out": u}, param_blobs={"statistic": "e"}
            )
            t.factors[f"goal{k}"] = FactorSpec(
                f"goal{k}", "categorical", edges={"out": x}, param_blobs={"statistic": "c"}
            )
            if gfe:
                detail = [("substituted_role", "out")]
                if learned_a:
                    detail.append(("parameter_uncertainty", "dirichlet"))
                t.constraints.append(
                    ConstraintSpec(ConstraintKind.P_SUBSTITUTION, f"obs{k}", tuple(sorted(detail)))
                )
            if map_policy:
                t.constraints.append(ConstraintSpec(ConstraintKind.DELTA, u))
        prev = zt
    t.ports["horizon"] = PortSpec("horizon", prev, PortRole.GLUE)  # open half-edge

    arrays = {
        "d": d,
        "A": A,
        "Ac": np.ones_like(A),  # placeholder counts; swapped at runtime
        "c": c,
        "e": e,
        "Bs": Bs,
    }
    return t, arrays

2

4	transition into z, an equality node exposing z to the observation branch and

rollout ellipses.

import numpy as np
import pytest

from cffg.core.ir import ConstraintKind, ConstraintSpec, Template, VariableSpec
from cffg.models.rollout import build_rollout
from cffg.viz import BeadShape, NodeEnd, TerminalEnd, TerminalKind, derive


def rollout(**kw):
    K, M, U = 4, 3, 2
    template, _ = build_rollout(
        "roll",
        steps=kw.pop("steps", 2),
        past=kw.pop("past", 0),
        d=np.full(K, 1 / K),
        A=np.full((M, K), 1 / M),
        c=np.full(M, 1 / M),
        e=np.full(U, 1 / U),
        Bs=np.stack([np.eye(K)] * U),
        **kw,
    )
    return template


class TestHmmSlice:
    def test_equality_node_is_default(self, hmm_slice):
        d = derive(hmm_slice)
        eq = d.nodes["eq"]
        assert eq.default_factorisation
        assert eq.groups == (pytest.approx,) or len(eq.groups) == 1
        assert eq.groups[0].roles == ("a", "b", "c")
        assert eq.groups[0].shape is BeadShape.CIRCLE

    def test_blob_bound_node_loses_default(self, hmm_slice):
        d = derive(hmm_slice)
        trans = d.nodes["trans"]
        assert trans.pointmass_roles == ("matrix",)
        assert not trans.default_factorisation  # the f_d case, Fig 16
        assert trans.groups == (pytest.approx,) or trans.groups[0].roles == ("out", "in")

    def test_data_clamped_role_leaves_q(self, hmm_slice):
        d = derive(hmm_slice)
        obs = d.nodes["obs"]
        assert set(obs.pointmass_roles) == {"out", "matrix"}  # x clamped + A blob
        assert obs.groups[0].roles == ("in",)

    def test_wire_terminals(self, hmm_slice):
        d = derive(hmm_slice)
        x = d.wires["var:x"]
        (term,) = [e for e in x.ends if isinstance(e, TerminalEnd)]
        assert term.kind is TerminalKind.DATA and term.ref == "port:sense"
        assert x.bead is None  # data constraint: pointmass, not a q bead

        for port in ("head", "tail"):
            var = hmm_slice.ports[port].variable
            (term,) = [
                e for e in d.wires[f"var:{var}"].ends if isinstance(e, TerminalEnd)
            ]
            assert term.kind is TerminalKind.ELLIPSIS  # glue: graph continues

        blob = d.wires["blob:trans.matrix"]
        (term,) = [e for e in blob.ends if isinstance(e, TerminalEnd)]
        assert term.kind is TerminalKind.POINTMASS and term.label == "B"
        assert blob.bead is None

    def test_internal_wire_has_default_bead(self, hmm_slice):
        d = derive(hmm_slice)
        z = d.wires["var:z_mid"]
        assert z.bead == ""  # empty normalisation bead
        assert {e.factor for e in z.node_ends()} == {"trans", "eq"}

        d = derive(rollout(gfe=True))
        for k in (1, 2):
            obs = d.nodes[f"obs{k}"]
            squares = [g for g in obs.groups if g.shape is BeadShape.SQUARE]
            assert [g.roles for g in squares] == [("out",)]
        assert [(c.members, c.x_variable) for c in d.composites] == [
            (("obs1", "goal1"), "x1"),
            (("obs2", "goal2"), "x2"),
        ]

    def test_no_gfe_means_no_squares_no_composites(self):
        d = derive(rollout(gfe=False))
        assert d.composites == []
        assert all(
            g.shape is BeadShape.CIRCLE for n in d.nodes.values() for g in n.groups
        )

    def test_map_policy_delta_bead_on_control_wire(self):
        d = derive(rollout(map_policy=True))
        assert d.wires["var:u1"].bead == "delta"  # Fig 29's MAP readout
        assert d.wires["var:zt1"].bead == ""

    def test_perception_slice_ports(self):
        d = derive(rollout(steps=2, past=1))
        for wire_id in ("var:u1", "var:x1"):
            (term,) = [
                e for e in d.wires[wire_id].ends if isinstance(e, TerminalEnd)
            ]
            assert term.kind is TerminalKind.DATA
        # planning slice unchanged
        assert d.composites and d.composites[0].members == ("obs2", "goal2")

    def test_horizon_glue_renders_as_ellipsis(self):
        d = derive(rollout())
        (term,) = [
            e for e in d.wires["var:zt2"].ends if isinstance(e, TerminalEnd)
        ]
        assert term.kind is TerminalKind.ELLIPSIS


class TestEdgeCases:

        assert [g.roles for g in d.nodes["eq"].groups] == [("a",), ("b",), ("c",)]

        t = Template(name="bad", variables={"loose": VariableSpec("loose", 2)})
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="loose"):
            derive(t)

"""CFFG compression (Part I §5.6, p.19) as presentation directives.

The recipe's four passes turn the fully-annotated diagram into the compact
form the papers use for real models. Level k applies passes 1..k:

1. Summarise bead chains by their terminating beads — empty on-wire
   normalisation beads disappear (symbol-carrying beads and terminals stay).
2. Nodes with no factorisation constraints lose their empty internal beads.
3. The same nodes lose their internal edge extensions (bare boxes).
4. All remaining internal beads are pushed to the node border; boxes shrink.

"No factorisation constraints" is `NodeView.default_factorisation`: a joint
marginal over *all* edges. A node with a pointmass edge (parameter blob or
data clamp) is not default — its q-marginal omits that edge — so it keeps its
beads, exactly the f_d case in Figs 16-17.

Passes never change *what the diagram means*, only what is drawn; hence they
produce directives over the semantic model rather than a mutated copy.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum

from cffg.viz.diagram import BeadGroup, Diagram

FULL_COMPRESSION = 4


class Placement(str, Enum):
    INTERNAL = "internal"  # beads inside the box, wires extended through the border
    BORDER = "border"  # beads straddle the border at their edges' attachment
    # points; multi-role groups render as an arc/dome spanning them (Fig 19)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NodeDirective:
    groups: tuple[BeadGroup, ...]  # beads actually drawn
    placement: Placement
    internal_edges: bool  # draw the edge extensions through the border


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WireDirective:
    bead: bool  # draw the on-wire bead at the wire midpoint
    symbol: str  # "" empty, "delta", ...


@dataclass
class Presentation:
    """What to draw, per element, at one compression level. Geometry-free:
    the layout stage consumes this together with the Diagram itself."""

    level: int
    compact: bool  # shrink boxes (pass 4's payoff, Fig 19 right)
    nodes: dict[str, NodeDirective]
    wires: dict[str, WireDirective]


def present(diagram: Diagram, level: int = FULL_COMPRESSION) -> Presentation:
    if not 0 <= level <= FULL_COMPRESSION:
        raise ValueError(f"compression level must be 0..4, got {level}")

    nodes: dict[str, NodeDirective] = {}
    for name, node in diagram.nodes.items():
        groups = node.groups
        if level >= 2 and node.default_factorisation:
            groups = tuple(g for g in groups if g.symbol)  # pass 2
        stripped = level >= 3 and node.default_factorisation and not groups  # pass 3
        nodes[name] = NodeDirective(
            groups=groups,
            placement=Placement.BORDER if level >= 4 else Placement.INTERNAL,
            internal_edges=level < 4 and not stripped,
        )

    wires: dict[str, WireDirective] = {}
    for wid, wire in diagram.wires.items():
        if wire.bead is None:  # pointmass wires never carry a q bead
            wires[wid] = WireDirective(bead=False, symbol="")
        else:  # pass 1: only symbol-carrying beads survive
            drawn = wire.bead != "" or level < 1
            wires[wid] = WireDirective(bead=drawn, symbol=wire.bead)

    return Presentation(
        level=level, compact=level >= FULL_COMPRESSION, nodes=nodes, wires=wires
    )

"""Compression passes (Part I p.19) as presentation directives.

Each test pins one pass to the figure that illustrates it (Figs 14-19)."""

import numpy as np
import pytest

from cffg.models.rollout import build_rollout
from cffg.viz import derive
from cffg.viz.compress import Placement, present


@pytest.fixture
def hmm(hmm_slice):
    return derive(hmm_slice)


def test_level_bounds(hmm):
    for bad in (-1, 5):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="level"):
            present(hmm, bad)


def test_pass1_empty_wire_beads_vanish(hmm):
    # Fig 15: the empty normalisation bead on the internal z_mid edge goes.
    assert present(hmm, 0).wires["var:z_mid"].bead
    for level in range(1, 5):
        assert not present(hmm, level).wires["var:z_mid"].bead


def test_pass1_keeps_symbol_beads():
    K, U, M = 4, 2, 3
    template, _ = build_rollout(
        "roll", steps=1,
        d=np.full(K, 1 / K), A=np.full((M, K), 1 / M), c=np.full(M, 1 / M),
        e=np.full(U, 1 / U), Bs=np.stack([np.eye(K)] * U), map_policy=True,
    )
    p = present(derive(template), 4)
    assert p.wires["var:u1"].bead and p.wires["var:u1"].symbol == "delta"


def test_pass2_default_nodes_lose_internal_beads(hmm):
    # Fig 16: eq has default factorisation, its joint bead goes; trans has a
    # pointmass parameter edge (the f_d case) so its bead stays.
    assert present(hmm, 1).nodes["eq"].groups
    for level in (2, 3, 4):
        p = present(hmm, level)
        assert p.nodes["eq"].groups == ()
        assert p.nodes["trans"].groups


def test_pass3_default_nodes_lose_internal_edges(hmm):
    # Fig 17: eq's extensions go; trans keeps its internal edges until pass 4.
    assert present(hmm, 2).nodes["eq"].internal_edges
    p3 = present(hmm, 3)
    assert not p3.nodes["eq"].internal_edges
    assert p3.nodes["trans"].internal_edges


def test_pass4_pushes_beads_to_border(hmm):
    # Figs 18-19: surviving beads straddle the border, boxes go compact.
    p3, p4 = present(hmm, 3), present(hmm, 4)
    assert p3.nodes["trans"].placement is Placement.INTERNAL and not p3.compact
    assert p4.nodes["trans"].placement is Placement.BORDER and p4.compact
    assert all(not d.internal_edges for d in p4.nodes.values())


def test_level0_is_uncompressed(hmm):
    p = present(hmm, 0)
    assert all(d.groups or n == "eq" for n, d in p.nodes.items())
    assert p.nodes["eq"].groups  # even default nodes show their joint bead
    assert p.wires["var:z_mid"].bead
    assert not p.wires["blob:trans.matrix"].bead  # pointmass: never a bead

"""Scene graph: typed drawable primitives with pixel coordinates.

The layout stage produces a Scene; backends (SVG today, an interactive GUI
later) consume it. Every item carries a `ref` back to the template element it
depicts ("factor:tm1", "var:x2", "blob:A", "port:sense", "gfe:obs1") so a
GUI can hit-test a primitive and resolve it to the model — the scene is the
contract that keeps renderers dumb.

Coordinates are y-down pixels; (0, 0) is the top-left of the canvas.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum

from cffg.viz.diagram import BeadShape, TerminalKind


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Box:
    """A factor node: square outline, glyph centered, name for tooltips."""

    ref: str
    x: float  # center
    y: float  # center
    w: float
    h: float
    glyph: str
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Path:
    """An open polyline (a wire, or an internal edge extension). Corners are
    bend points; backends may round them (the papers' quarter-arc corners)."""

    ref: str
    points: tuple[tuple[float, float], ...]
    kind: str = "wire"  # "wire" | "internal"
    label: str = ""
    label_at: tuple[float, float] | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Bead:
    """A q-marginal bead: on a wire, inside a box, or straddling its border."""

    ref: str
    x: float
    y: float
    shape: BeadShape
    symbol: str = ""  # "", "delta", "E", ...
    filled: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Dome:
    """A joint node-marginal bead pushed to the border (Fig 19): an arc
    through `anchors` (the member edges' attachment points) bulging into the
    box toward (cx, cy)."""

    ref: str
    anchors: tuple[tuple[float, float], ...]
    cx: float
    cy: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Terminal:
    """A wire ending: pointmass square, filled data bead, or open bead."""

    ref: str
    x: float
    y: float
    kind: TerminalKind
    label: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EllipsisMark:
    """Continuation dots at a glue port: the model rolls out further."""

    ref: str
    x: float
    y: float
    angle: float = 0.0  # degrees; 0 = horizontal continuation


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CompositeBox:
    """Dashed rounded box around a GFE composite's members."""

    ref: str
    x: float  # top-left
    y: float
    w: float
    h: float


class ItemKind(str, Enum):
    pass  # reserved: scenes are heterogeneous lists, discriminated by type


SceneItem = Box | Path | Bead | Dome | Terminal | EllipsisMark | CompositeBox


@dataclass
class Scene:
    """The drawable result: items in painter's order (first = bottom)."""

    name: str
    width: float
    height: float
    items: list[SceneItem] = field(default_factory=list)

    def by_ref(self, ref: str) -> list[SceneItem]:
        return [i for i in self.items if i.ref == ref]

    def boxes(self) -> dict[str, Box]:
        return {i.ref: i for i in self.items if isinstance(i, Box)}

"""Scene graph: typed drawable primitives with pixel coordinates.

The layout stage produces a Scene; backends (SVG today, an interactive GUI
later) consume it. Every item carries a `ref` back to the template element it
depicts ("factor:tm1", "var:x2", "blob:A", "port:sense", "gfe:obs1") so a
GUI can hit-test a primitive and resolve it to the model — the scene is the
contract that keeps renderers dumb.

Coordinates are y-down pixels; (0, 0) is the top-left of the canvas.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum

from cffg.viz.diagram import BeadShape, TerminalKind


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Box:
    """A factor node: square outline, glyph centered, name for tooltips."""

    ref: str
    x: float  # center
    y: float  # center
    w: float
    h: float
    glyph: str
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Path:
    """An open polyline (a wire, or an internal edge extension). Corners are
    bend points; backends may round them (the papers' quarter-arc corners)."""

    ref: str
    points: tuple[tuple[float, float], ...]
    kind: str = "wire"  # "wire" | "internal"
    label: str = ""
    label_at: tuple[float, float] | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Bead:
    """A q-marginal bead: on a wire, inside a box, or straddling its border."""

    ref: str
    x: float
    y: float
    shape: BeadShape
    symbol: str = ""  # "", "delta", "E", ...
    filled: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Dome:
    """A joint node-marginal bead pushed to the border (Fig 19): an arc
    through `anchors` (the member edges' attachment points) bulging into the
    box toward (cx, cy)."""

    ref: str
    anchors: tuple[tuple[float, float], ...]
    cx: float
    cy: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Terminal:
    """A wire ending: pointmass square, filled data bead, or open bead."""

    ref: str
    x: float
    y: float
    kind: TerminalKind
    label: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EllipsisMark:
    """Continuation dots at a glue port: the model rolls out further."""

    ref: str
    x: float
    y: float
    angle: float = 0.0  # degrees; 0 = horizontal continuation


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CompositeBox:
    """Dashed rounded box around a GFE composite's members."""

    ref: str
    x: float  # top-left
    y: float
    w: float
    h: float


class ItemKind(str, Enum):
    pass  # reserved: scenes are heterogeneous lists, discriminated by type


SceneItem = Box | Path | Bead | Dome | Terminal | EllipsisMark | CompositeBox


@dataclass
class Scene:
    """The drawable result: items in painter's order (first = bottom)."""

    name: str
    width: float
    height: float
    items: list[SceneItem] = field(default_factory=list)

    def by_ref(self, ref: str) -> list[SceneItem]:
        return [i for i in self.items if i.ref == ref]

    def boxes(self) -> dict[str, Box]:
        return {i.ref: i for i in self.items if isinstance(i, Box)}

    """The border-pushed joint bead (Fig 19): one quadratic between the two
    farthest anchors — a dome for opposite sides, a corner-rounding curve for
    adjacent ones — plus straight stubs joining any remaining anchors to it."""
    anchors = sorted(item.anchors)
    pairs = [(a, b) for i, a in enumerate(anchors) for b in anchors[i + 1 :]]
    a, b = max(pairs, key=lambda p: _dist(*p))
    rest = [p for p in anchors if p not in (a, b)]
    mx, my = (a[0] + b[0]) / 2, (a[1] + b[1]) / 2

    if abs(a[0] - b[0]) < 1.0 or abs(a[1] - b[1]) < 1.0:  # opposite sides
        if rest:  # bulge away from the remaining anchors
            rx = sum(p[0] for p in rest) / len(rest) - mx
            ry = sum(p[1] for p in rest) / len(rest) - my
            n = hypot(rx, ry) or 1.0

        elif abs(a[1] - b[1]) < 1.0:
            ux, uy = 0.0, 1.0  # horizontal chord: dome opens downward (Fig 22)

        half = _dist(a, b) / 2
        cx, cy = mx + ux * half * 1.6, my + uy * half * 1.6
    else:  # adjacent sides: hug the shared corner (the f_d look, Fig 19)
        cx = a[0] if abs(a[0] - item.cx) > abs(b[0] - item.cx) else b[0]
        cy = a[1] if abs(a[1] - item.cy) > abs(b[1] - item.cy) else b[1]

"""Grid layout: rail extraction, branch sides, terminal placement, stability.

The claims mirror the papers' layout conventions (Figs 22/26): time reads
left to right along the state chain, control priors sit above it, the
observation/goal stack hangs below, and — the editing property — growing a
model only adds rows/columns, never moves what was already there.
"""

import pytest

from cffg.models.rollout import build_rollout
from cffg.viz import derive
from cffg.viz.compress import present
from cffg.viz.diagram import TerminalKind
from cffg.viz.layout import LayoutStyle, layout

def rollout_template(steps=2, **kw):
    K, M, U = 4, 3, 2

"""SVG backend: well-formedness, paper notation coverage, golden files.

Goldens pin the full pipeline for the canonical models. After a deliberate
visual change, regenerate with:

    CFFG_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/test_viz_svg.py
"""

import os
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from cffg.models.tmaze import build_tmaze
from cffg.viz import render_svg, save_svg

GOLDEN = Path(__file__).parent / "golden"


def elements(svg: str, tag: str) -> list:
    root = ET.fromstring(svg)  # raises on malformed XML
    return [e for e in root.iter() if e.tag.endswith(f"}}{tag}")]


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def tmaze():
    return build_tmaze()[0]


def test_svg_is_well_formed_at_every_level(tmaze):
    for level in range(5):
        ET.fromstring(render_svg(tmaze, level=level))


def test_notation_inventory(tmaze):
    svg = render_svg(tmaze, level=4)
    texts = [t.text for t in elements(svg, "text") if t.text]
    assert "Cat" in texts and "TM" in texts and "=" in texts
    # 2 planning slices: 2 dashed composite boxes + 2 P-substitution squares
    rects = elements(svg, "rect")
    assert sum(1 for r in rects if r.get("stroke-dasharray")) == 2
    squares = [r for r in rects if r.get("width") == r.get("height") == "12.0"]
    assert len(squares) == 2
    # subscripts render as absolute-size tspans (cairosvg chokes on %)
    assert all("%" not in (t.get("font-size") or "") for t in elements(svg, "tspan"))


def test_compression_removes_beads(tmaze):
    full = len(elements(render_svg(tmaze, level=0), "circle"))
    compressed = len(elements(render_svg(tmaze, level=4), "circle"))
    assert compressed < full


def test_save_svg(tmaze, tmp_path):
    out = save_svg(tmaze, tmp_path / "tmaze.svg")
    assert out.read_text().startswith("<svg")


def test_render_is_deterministic(tmaze):
    assert render_svg(tmaze) == render_svg(tmaze)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "name,level",
    [("hmm_slice", 0), ("hmm_slice", 4), ("tmaze", 4)],
)
def test_golden(name, level, hmm_slice, tmaze):
    template = {"hmm_slice": hmm_slice, "tmaze": tmaze}[name]
    svg = render_svg(template, level=level)
    path = GOLDEN / f"{name}_l{level}.svg"
    if os.environ.get("CFFG_UPDATE_GOLDENS"):
        path.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(svg)
    assert path.exists(), "golden missing; run with CFFG_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1"
    assert svg == path.read_text(), (
        f"render drifted from {path.name}; if intended, regenerate with "
        "CFFG_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1"
    )

# cffg

Constrained Forney-style Factor Graphs (CFFG) and Lagrangian Active Inference
(LAIF) in JAX — an engine for building **white-box probabilistic agents**:
models you can read, edit, checkpoint, and ship, whose exploration comes from
their objective (Generalised Free Energy) rather than bolted-on noise.

Implements Koudahl, van de Laar & de Vries, *Realising Synthetic Active
Inference Agents* Parts I & II (arXiv:2306.08014), validated to 1.7e-6
against the authors' Julia reference on the T-maze benchmark.

```sh
uv sync          # install
uv run pytest    # 105 tests; the T-maze + gridworld suites are living examples
```

## The mental model

A model is a **Template**: a factor graph (square factors, edges = variables)
plus **constraint beads** that pick the variational objective, plus typed
**ports** where the world plugs in.

| Piece | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `VariableSpec` | a discrete random variable (an edge; connects ≤ 2 factors) |
| `FactorSpec` | a distribution node: `categorical`, `matrix_cat`, `transition_mixture`, `equality`, `dirichlet` |
| `ConstraintSpec` | a bead: `P_SUBSTITUTION` (adds the epistemic/GFE drive), `DELTA` (MAP readout), `MEAN_FIELD` (VMP) |
| `PortSpec` | a dangling edge with a role: `data` (sensor), `goal`, `prior`, `glue` (composition) |

The load-bearing invariant: every variable is either fully connected or
exposed through exactly one port — so "no dangling edges" and "models
compose" are the same rule.

**The one bead that matters most:** `P_SUBSTITUTION` on an observation factor
facing a goal factor turns that pair into a GFE composite — the agent then
*values information* about that observation. Without it you get a KL-control
agent that never explores (we test this: same graph, one bead, 90% vs 0% on
the T-maze).

## Build a model

For the common case — a discrete POMDP over a time window — one call:

```python
import numpy as np
from cffg.models.rollout import build_rollout

template, arrays = build_rollout(
    "my_world",
    steps=3,          # slices in the window
    past=0,           # slices 1..past are perception (data ports act{k}/obs{k})
    d=d,              # prior over the initial state          [K]
    A=A,              # observation model, column-stochastic   [M, K]
    c=c,              # goal prior over observations           [M]
    e=e,              # control prior                          [U]
    Bs=Bs,            # per-control transitions, col-stochastic [U, K, K]
    gfe=True,         # P-beads on future observations (curiosity on)
)
```

`cffg.models.tmaze` and `cffg.models.gridworld` are two worked instances of
this. For custom topologies, build the `Template` by hand (see
`tests/conftest.py` for a hand-built HMM slice) and grow big models from
small ones:

```python
from cffg.core.compose import unroll, compose
chain = unroll(slice_template, 10, {"tail": "head"})     # glue-port chaining
model = compose(prior_template, chain, {"attach": "t0/head"}, name="hmm10")
```

## Run inference

```python
from cffg.compiler import compile_template
from cffg.engine import Engine

engine = Engine(compile_template(template, arrays=arrays))
state  = engine.init_state()
state  = engine.bind_data(state, {"obs1": 4, "obs2": None})   # clamp / missing
state, deltas = engine.run(state, 200, tol=1e-12, damp=0.5)   # flood to coherence

engine.marginals(state)["u1"]   # posteriors by variable name
engine.bfe(state)               # exact Bethe/Generalised free energy
```

Rules of thumb: `damp=0.5` whenever the model has ≥ 2 GFE composites (their
outer coordination can limit-cycle undamped); `deltas` is the coherence
signal — trees converge hard, so treat a plateau as a smell. On tree graphs
`bfe` equals −log evidence exactly; with no data it is 0 for a normalized
model — both make good sanity checks. Parameters are *inputs* (`state.params`),
so you can swap them per run without recompiling.

## Run an agent

```python
import functools
from cffg.agent import RollingAgent
from cffg.models.gridworld import CorridorEnv, build_gridworld

env   = CorridorEnv(k=6, seed=1)
agent = RollingAgent(functools.partial(build_gridworld, k=6), horizon=3)
for _ in range(10):
    action, observation = agent.step(env.step)   # plan → act → filter belief

agent.checkpoint("agent.npz"); agent.restore("agent.npz")
```

Two compiled engines cover any episode length: a planning window from the
current belief and a one-slice filter that re-anchors it. Pass
`learn_a=True, initial_counts=...` for continual Dirichlet learning of the
observation model (see `cffg/experiments/tmaze_learning.py` for the full
perception–action–learning cycle reproducing Part II Fig. 9).

Many agents on one machine:

```python
from cffg.colony import Colony
colony = Colony()
ids = [colony.spawn(t, arrays_i) for arrays_i in per_instance_params]
colony.run(100, damp=0.5)      # one vmapped step-loop per unique structure
colony.marginals(ids[0])
```

Engines are cached by structure hash — N instances of one template cost one
compilation, and instances couple only through their ports.

four-stage pipeline, each stage importable on its own:

   stability property a template editor needs.

content.text:
The plotting facility is done and landed — six commits on `main`, epic `cff-ql2n` closed, tree clean, 143 tests green (25 new), dashboard refreshed.

## What got built

`cffg/viz/` — a four-stage pipeline where each stage is independently usable:

1. **`derive`** (diagram.py) — maps a `Template` onto the paper's visual algebra: the default variational spec made explicit (joint bead per node, normalisation bead per internal edge), then perturbed per the notation — mean-field splits beads, `P_SUBSTITUTION` becomes a square bead, `DELTA` puts ∂ on the wire, `param_blobs` become black pointmass terminals, data ports become filled terminating beads, glue ports become `⋯` rollout ellipses, and GFE composites (detected the same way the compiler does) get dashed boxes.
2. **`present`** (compress.py) — Part I p.19's four compression passes as levels 0–4, including the subtle f_d rule: a node with a pointmass edge keeps its beads at every level.
3. **`layout`** — deterministic rectilinear grid mirroring the paper's conventions: glue-anchored rail left→right, control priors above, obs/goal stacks below, parameter terminals on the first free side (which lands **d**, **A**, **B**, **c**, **e** exactly where Figs 22/26 put them). Placement is a pure function of names/topology, and there's a regression test proving that growing a rollout from 2 to 3 steps moves *zero* existing boxes.
4. **`scene` / `svg`** — a typed scene graph whose every primitive carries a `factor:`/`var:`/`port:` ref (your future GUI hit-tests against this), serialized to paper-style SVG: serif italic labels with subscripts, quarter-arc wire corners, border domes.

The rendered T-maze at level 4 is essentially a reproduction of Figure 26 — dome'd TM nodes with the u-wire stub, bare `=` nodes, T-with-square-bead composites, the works. Level 0 gives the Fig 14 all-beads view. I verified both visually against the paper pages, plus the gridworld at 3 steps.

## Usage

```python
from cffg.viz import render_svg, save_svg, save_png, build_scene
save_svg(template, "model.svg")        # level=4 default; level=0..4 available
save_png(template, "model.png")        # optional extra: uv sync --extra viz
```

Per your choices: SVG core is dependency-free, PNG lives behind the `viz` extra, and full compression is the default. One machine note: cairosvg needs brew's cairo on the dyld path (`DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/homebrew/lib`) — recorded in the epic's handoff note.

## Left open

`cff-jude` (backlog, unblocked): the message-passing schedule overlay from Figs 23/24/27 — the scene graph already anchors overlays to wires by ref, so it slots in cleanly when you want it. README and ARCHITECTURE.md both document the new component.

import pytest

from cffg.core import (
    BlobRef,
    FactorSpec,
    PortRole,
    PortSpec,
    Template,
    VariableSpec,
)

# Rendered-diagram gallery: tests record SVGs here (gitignored); the dashboard
# (tools/dashboard.py) picks them up and shows them under the matching test row.
VIZ_ARTIFACTS = Path(__file__).parent / ".artifacts"


def pytest_sessionstart(session):
    shutil.rmtree(VIZ_ARTIFACTS, ignore_errors=True)


@pytest.fixture
def viz_gallery(request):
    """Record diagrams this test produces: `viz_gallery(template, level=4,
    tag="...")`. Accepts a Template (rendered via cffg.viz) or a ready SVG
    string. Each image gets a JSON sidecar naming the test, so the dashboard
    can attach it to the right row without any registry to maintain."""

    from cffg.viz import render_svg

    file = Path(request.node.location[0]).name
    test_id = f"{file}::{request.node.name}"
    slug = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "-", f"{Path(file).stem}-{request.node.name}")
    count = iter(range(100))

    def record(template_or_svg, *, level=4, tag=""):
        svg = (
            template_or_svg
            if isinstance(template_or_svg, str)
            else render_svg(template_or_svg, level=level)
        )
        suffix = f"-{tag}" if tag else ""
        stem = f"{slug}-{next(count):02d}{re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+', '-', suffix)}"
        VIZ_ARTIFACTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        (VIZ_ARTIFACTS / f"{stem}.svg").write_text(svg)
        (VIZ_ARTIFACTS / f"{stem}.json").write_text(
            json.dumps({"id": test_id, "tag": tag})
        )

    return record
